messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: unusual auth activity detected on auth-prod. Spike in 401/403 + tokens seen from multiple regions within <1min window. Rule=auth.session_propagation_high. Alert id=ALG-1971. Runbook: #incidents -> auth triage.
oncall-jen: I'm on it, grabbing context and will assemble a triage group.
Maria R: seeing 2.3k auth failures last 5m, 78 distinct tokens with same opaque token reused across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Hash looks like user-session token, not API key.
Chris P: which service reported reuse? auth-proxy vs session-store?
Maria R: auth-proxy ingress logs show reuse, session-store shows single token mapping to 3 different client IPs at same minute.
sec-lee: this smells like session replay or token leak. We should assume token exfil until proven otherwise. Actions: 1) rotate session signing key if possible, 2) bulk-revoke tokens issued before cutover, 3) block suspicious IPs, 4) collect and persist sample logs for forensics.
Mike T: I can run quick revocation for affected tenants. Need list of token ids or issued_at cutoff. Maria, can you export token ids for last 10m?
Maria R: exporting now. sample token ids: tkn_3b9f..., tkn_6aa2..., tkn_f0c1... (redacted). Issued_at cutoff: 2026-03-15T18:04:00Z.
Sam B: tagging compliance and legal for telemetry retention and PII handling. @sec-lee do we need to notify any customers now?
sec-lee: risk-based: if tokens allow access to customer data, high priority customers first. Start with customers with active sessions correlated to these tokens. Prepare a status draft but wait until we know actual data access.
oncall-jen: I'll run the rotate key playbook. Steps in runbook:
```
# rotate session signing key (short lived)
POST /admin/keys/rotate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"key_type":"session_signing"}'
# set new key active, keep old key for verify for 5m, then revoke
```
Maria R: note: session-store uses HMAC secret K1 on auth-prod-1. If we rotate K1 we need to invalidate caches across regions. Expected user impact: forced re-login for active sessions.
Chris P: alternative: selectively revoke tokens in the sampled list to minimize blast radius. We can throttle revocation by tenant.
sec-lee: agreed: do revocation first for tokens seen reused and for tenants flagged as high-sensitivity (finance, healthcare). Rotate global key if evidence grows.
Mike T: kicked off revocation job for 42 tokens across 8 tenants. Job id=rev-1971-01. Command used:
```
POST /admin/sessions/revoke_batch
{"tokens": ["tkn_3b9f...","tkn_6aa2..."], "reason":"suspected_replay"}
```
Maria R: also found 3 entries in debug logs that contain stack traces with truncated session token fragments — likely accidental logging from a legacy debug path. File paths: auth-proxy/debug/2026-03-15/18:03/*.log. Preserving copies to secure S3 bucket redwood-sec-inquiry.
sec-lee: log exposure -> treat as potential leak. Purge debug logs, rotate any keys that may be in those logs, and run a search for other paths. I'll open a forensic ticket.
Sam B: created ticket SEC-1971 for forensics and privacy review. Assigned to @sec-lee and @legal.
oncall-jen: quick mitigation status: revoked known reused tokens (42), blocked 12 suspicious IPs at edge WAF, alerted CDN to throttle suspicious UA patterns. Next: decide on global signing key rotation.
Maria R: telemetry shows user impact: ~1.4k end-users will be forced to re-auth over next hour (mostly mobile apps). Customer-facing impact estimate: 0.6% of monthly active users, likely minor but visible.
Chris P: ops question: do we want to push a status page update now or wait for confirmation?
sec-lee: post an initial status update: "Investigating unusual authentication activity; mitigation in progress. Some users may be required to re-login. We will provide updates." No mention of leaked logs specifics yet.
Mike T: status incident doc started at https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1971 (placeholder). Adding runbook outputs and revoked token ids.
Sam B: communications: draft message ready for top-tier customers if they ask. Template: we forced session invalidation and recommending rotation of OAuth app secrets if you use them.
Maria R: after sampling more logs, evidence points to a debug env misconfig that forwarded truncated tokens to a logging endpoint that was indexed publicly for a short window. We'll continue forensics.
sec-lee: ordering: 1) preserve logs and lock down S3 bucket (done), 2) finish targeted token revocations (in progress), 3) rotate any exposed service keys (pending inventory), 4) decide on global session key rotation. If legal wants customer notification, loop back.
oncall-jen: handing off to next oncall in 30m: @Mike T will continue mitigation and @sec-lee will lead forensic. I'll update PagerDuty with handoff note. :thumbsup:
Mike T: acknowledged, will monitor revocation job and update here every 15m.
sec-lee: noted, I'll run a quick sensitive-data search across logs and start our breach checklist if PII is found.
Sam B: will prepare customer comms and status page update, timeline ~45m for initial public status.
Maria R: final note for the thread: keep all evidence in SEC-1971 and avoid copying PII into Slack.
Chris P: thanks team, ping me if we need to escalate to rotating global keys.
incident-bot: Incident update: ALG-1971 -> severity=high, status=mitigating, pagerduty=acknowledged.
